extracted.intended_audience: social-impact leaders, organizations, and changemakers seeking funding or partnership with The Audacious Project
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit selection standards used by The Audacious Project to source, shape, review, fund, and launch finalist projects addressing global problems. Applies to changemakers preparing proposals or partners nominating projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boldness / scale of idea
rubrics_metrics.description: Match bold ideas with catalytic resources; surface their boldest ideas for tackling global problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Audacious Project seeks ideas that are ambitious in scope and aim to address major global challenges. Language on the page explicitly encourages changemakers to 'dream bigger than ever before.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Viable multi-year plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Help shape their best ideas into viable multi-year plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should articulate an executable multi-year strategy — not just a concept. The program offers support to shape ideas into multi-year plans, implying that applicants need a plan that is realistic over multiple years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling presentation to supporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Present those solutions in a compelling way to potential supporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects must be framed and communicated so they persuade donors and the public; finalists receive support to make their case compelling for private donor briefings and public unveiling at TED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing pathway (public application or partner nomination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects are sourced from public applications and a global network of partners and donors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility for consideration is via public application or nomination/identification by partner organizations and donors. This indicates the practical routes by which projects enter the pipeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and issue-area representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalists' ideas are representative of a broad range of geographies and issue areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection aims for diversity across regions and problem domains; the shortlist is narrowed to finalists that collectively represent varied geographies and issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local leadership / proximity to served communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Elevating leaders with proximity to the communities they serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program favors and intentionally uplifts leaders who are close to or embedded in the communities impacted by the proposed work, emphasizing local leadership and lived-experience proximity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proven changemakers / track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Every year, we work with proven changemakers to surface their boldest ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection prioritizes applicants with demonstrated leadership or prior impact (‘proven changemakers’), suggesting that past performance or evidence of capability is an important criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous due diligence and ideation support
rubrics_metrics.description: Each finalist project goes through a rigorous due diligence, ideation and investment support process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalists are evaluated via a thorough due-diligence process and receive ideation/investment support to refine plans. Due diligence assesses feasibility, risks, assumptions, and readiness for donor investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility and persuasiveness (achievable and compelling proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure their proposal is achievable and compelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must demonstrate both practical feasibility (achievability) and a convincing case for impact (compelling narrative/metrics). This is an explicit objective of the ideation and investment support stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readiness for donor briefing and public launch
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalist projects are presented privately to groups of donors and are then publicly unveiled at TED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected projects should be prepared for private donor presentations and a high-profile public launch (TED), implying standards for polish, accountability, and public-facing communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to ongoing reporting and milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Funded projects then pursue their plans and share regular updates on key milestones reached with donors and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded teams are expected to continue implementation and provide regular milestone updates to donors and the public, indicating monitoring, transparency, and reporting obligations post-funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: External expert review and diverse perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: A diverse array of reviewers and expert perspectives are engaged each cycle to enrich understanding of project potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are reviewed by a changing but diverse network of experts (listed on the page), implying that proposals should anticipate scrutiny from domain experts and be prepared to respond to varied evaluative perspectives.
